# Setup and hourly imports

Keep `forecast_lab.py` alongside this file. In VS Code on Windows, install the kernel and libraries with `py -m pip install -r requirements.txt`, select the matching Python kernel, and run the chunks in order. Place the EIA regional workbooks under `data/`. Export Site settings to `settings.json` to reproduce a run. The final chunk is disabled until you approve the CV results and freeze the settings.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import json
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display
from forecast_lab import (
    CODES, DEFAULTS, build_training, diagnostics, read_project_files,
    run_cv, run_holdout, score, validate,
)

settings_file = Path("settings.json")
settings = json.loads(settings_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if settings_file.exists() else DEFAULTS
cfg = validate(settings)
sources = read_project_files({
    region: Path("data") / f"Region_{CODES[region]}.xlsx"
    for region in cfg["REGIONS"]
})
```

# Cleaning

## Hourly quality and daily averages

The daily target is mean valid hourly MW by local calendar date. The regional time zone determines whether a date expects 23, 24, or 25 hours. The optional California rule is scoped to November 2, 2024. Review the training audit before running CV. Missing daily targets are excluded from scoring. Model inputs use past values to fill gaps.

```{python}
training, checks = build_training(sources, cfg)
display(pd.DataFrame([
    {"Region": region, "Start": y.first_valid_index(), "End": y.last_valid_index(),
     "Observed days": y.notna().sum(), "Excluded days": y.isna().sum(),
     "DST dates": sum(row["expected"] != 24 for row in checks[region])}
    for region, y in training.items()
]))
```

# Training diagnostics

## Demand, weekly STL, and stationarity

Use ACF/PACF and ADF/KPSS together to inspect levels and differenced series. Review the output separately for each region. Change `region` to inspect another series. These checks support model interpretation, while CV estimates accuracy.

```{python}
region = cfg["REGIONS"][0]
y = training[region]
report = diagnostics(y)
if report:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 1, figsize=(11, 7), sharex=True)
    axes[0].plot(y, lw=.7)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Demand (MW)")
    for ax, name in zip(axes[1:], ["trend", "seasonal", "resid"]):
        ax.plot(pd.to_datetime(report["dates"]), report[name], lw=.7)
        ax.set_ylabel(name.title())
    plt.show()
    tests = report["stationarity"]
    display(pd.DataFrame(tests).T.drop(columns=["acf", "pacf"]))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3))
    for ax, name in zip(axes, ["acf", "pacf"]):
        ax.stem(tests["Level"][name])
        ax.set_title(name.upper())
        ax.set_xlabel("Daily lag")
    plt.show()
```

# Models and training cross-validation

Compare the weekly seasonal naïve benchmark, additive damped weekly ETS, ARIMA(1,1,1), and TSLM with trend, weekday indicators, and two annual Fourier pairs. Each expanding origin fits the same model specifications. CV uses training targets only, and the lowest MAE marks the CV winner per region and configured horizon. ME is actual minus forecast. MASE uses observed lag-7 absolute differences available at each origin.

```{python}
cv_rows, finalists, cv_info = run_cv(training, cfg)
display(pd.DataFrame(finalists))
cv_horizons = [row for row in cv_rows if row["day"] in cfg["HORIZONS"]]
display(score(cv_horizons, ["region", "day", "model"]))
```

# Final holdout

Freeze settings and model specifications before enabling this chunk. The rolling evaluation can use observations available by each origin to re-estimate model parameters. It uses the same specifications and the original CV winners. Only observed targets inside the evaluation window are scored.

```{python}
#| eval: false
holdout_rows, holdout_info = run_holdout(sources, training, cfg)
requested = [row for row in holdout_rows if row["day"] in cfg["HORIZONS"]]
display(score(requested, ["region", "day", "model"]))
daily_errors = score(holdout_rows, ["region", "target", "model"])
```

# Future demand predictions

After reviewing the final evaluation, refit the training-CV winner for the selected region and horizon on all usable observations. The forecast starts the day after that region's latest usable daily observation.

```{python}
#| eval: false
from forecast_lab import future_forecast

region = cfg["REGIONS"][0]
horizon = max(cfg["HORIZONS"])
future = future_forecast(sources, cfg, finalists, region, horizon)
predictions = pd.DataFrame(future["predictions"])
recent = pd.DataFrame(future["recent"], columns=["date", "observed_mw"])
forecast_line = pd.concat([
    recent.tail(1).rename(columns={"observed_mw": "predicted_mw"}),
    predictions[["date", "predicted_mw"]],
])
plt.plot(pd.to_datetime(recent["date"]), recent["observed_mw"], label="Observed")
plt.plot(pd.to_datetime(forecast_line["date"]), forecast_line["predicted_mw"],
         "--", label=f"Forecast ({future['model']})")
plt.axvline(pd.Timestamp(future["origin"]), color="gray", linestyle=":")
plt.ylabel("Daily average demand (MW)")
plt.legend()
plt.gcf().autofmt_xdate()
plt.show()
display(predictions)
```
## 8. Time Series Decomposition

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import display

from scipy import stats
from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import MSTL, STL
from statsmodels.graphics.tsaplots import plot_acf, plot_pacf
from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import acf, kpss
from statsmodels.tools.sm_exceptions import InterpolationWarning
import warnings
from forecast_lab import causal_fill

regions = sorted(training)
training_series = {}
for region in regions:
    y = causal_fill(training[region]).sort_index().asfreq("D")
    assert y.notna().all() and y.gt(0).all()
    assert y.index[-1] == pd.Timestamp(cfg["TRAIN_END"])
    if len(y) <= 730:
        raise ValueError(f"{region}: annual MSTL needs more than two years of training data.")
    training_series[region] = y


def component_strength(component, remainder):
    return max(0, 1 - remainder.var() / (remainder + component).var())


strength_rows = []
for region, y in training_series.items():
    weekly_stl = STL(y, period=7, robust=True).fit()
    multi_stl = MSTL(y, periods=(7, 365), stl_kwargs={"robust": True}).fit()
    strength_rows.append({
        "Region": region,
        "Weekly (STL)": component_strength(weekly_stl.seasonal, weekly_stl.resid),
        "Weekly (MSTL)": component_strength(multi_stl.seasonal["seasonal_7"], multi_stl.resid),
        "Annual (MSTL)": component_strength(multi_stl.seasonal["seasonal_365"], multi_stl.resid),
        "Trend (MSTL)": component_strength(multi_stl.trend, multi_stl.resid),
    })

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(5, 1, figsize=(10, 7), sharex=True)
    components = {
        "Observed": y,
        "Trend": multi_stl.trend,
        "Weekly": multi_stl.seasonal["seasonal_7"],
        "Annual": multi_stl.seasonal["seasonal_365"],
        "Remainder": multi_stl.resid,
    }
    for ax, (label, component) in zip(axes, components.items()):
        ax.plot(component.index, component, linewidth=0.7)
        ax.set_ylabel(label)
    axes[-1].set_xlabel("Training date")
    fig.supylabel("Daily average demand (MW)")
    fig.suptitle(f"{region} weekly and annual decomposition")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

strength = pd.DataFrame(strength_rows).set_index("Region")
display(strength.round(3))
for region, row in strength.iterrows():
    stronger = "annual" if row["Annual (MSTL)"] > row["Weekly (MSTL)"] else "weekly"
    print(f"{region}: weekly {row['Weekly (MSTL)']:.3f}, "
          f"annual {row['Annual (MSTL)']:.3f}, trend {row['Trend (MSTL)']:.3f}. "
          f"The {stronger} component has the higher seasonal strength.")
```

## 9. Feature Engineering

```{python}
annual_period = 365.25
first_day = min(y.index[0] for y in training_series.values())
weekday_cols = [f"weekday_{day}" for day in range(1, 7)]


def calendar_features(index, region, k):
    x = pd.DataFrame({"unique_id": region, "ds": index})
    elapsed = (x["ds"] - first_day).dt.days
    x["weekday"] = x["ds"].dt.day_of_week
    x["month"] = x["ds"].dt.month
    x["trend"] = elapsed / annual_period
    for day in range(1, 7):
        x[f"weekday_{day}"] = (x["weekday"] == day).astype(int)
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        angle = 2 * np.pi * i * elapsed / annual_period
        x[f"sin_{i}"] = np.sin(angle)
        x[f"cos_{i}"] = np.cos(angle)
    return x


analysis_horizon = max(cfg["HORIZONS"])
cv_origins = pd.date_range(
    max(y.index[0] for y in training_series.values())
    + pd.Timedelta(days=cfg["CV_INITIAL"] - 1),
    pd.Timestamp(cfg["TRAIN_END"]) - pd.Timedelta(days=analysis_horizon),
    freq=f"{cfg['CV_STEP']}D",
)
if not len(cv_origins):
    raise ValueError("No shared training CV origins. Review CV_INITIAL and training coverage.")

k_scores = []
for region, y in training_series.items():
    x = calendar_features(y.index, region, 3)
    actual = training[region].reindex(y.index).to_numpy()
    origin_rows = y.index.get_indexer(cv_origins)
    assert (origin_rows >= 0).all() and (origin_rows + analysis_horizon < len(y)).all()

    for k in (1, 2, 3):
        fourier_cols = [f"{term}_{i}" for i in range(1, k + 1) for term in ("sin", "cos")]
        columns = ["trend"] + weekday_cols + fourier_cols
        design = x[columns].assign(intercept=1).to_numpy()
        errors = []
        for row in origin_rows:
            split = row + 1
            stop = split + analysis_horizon
            coefficients = np.linalg.lstsq(design[:split], y.iloc[:split], rcond=None)[0]
            prediction = design[split:stop] @ coefficients
            observed = actual[split:stop]
            valid = np.isfinite(observed)
            errors.extend(np.abs((observed[valid] - prediction[valid]) / observed[valid]))
        k_scores.append({"Region": region, "K": k, "CV MAPE (%)": 100 * np.mean(errors),
                         "Scored targets": len(errors)})

k_scores = pd.DataFrame(k_scores)
mean_mape = k_scores.groupby("K")["CV MAPE (%)"].mean()
fourier_k = int(mean_mape.idxmin())
fourier_cols = [f"{term}_{i}" for i in range(1, fourier_k + 1) for term in ("sin", "cos")]
arima_x_cols = weekday_cols + fourier_cols
tslm_x_cols = ["trend"] + arima_x_cols

display(k_scores.round(3))
print(f"Selected shared K = {fourier_k} across {len(cv_origins)} training origins.")
print(f"Mean regional CV MAPE: {mean_mape.loc[fourier_k]:.3f}%.")
train_features = pd.concat([
    calendar_features(y.index, region, fourier_k)
    for region, y in training_series.items()
], ignore_index=True)
```

## 10. Post-Feature Engineering EDA

```{python}
holdout_dates = pd.date_range(cfg["TEST_START"], cfg["TEST_END"], freq="D")
future_features = pd.concat([
    calendar_features(holdout_dates, region, fourier_k)
    for region in regions
], ignore_index=True)
X_df = future_features[["unique_id", "ds"] + arima_x_cols].copy()

feature_checks = []
for label, features in [("Training", train_features), ("Holdout calendar", future_features)]:
    assert not features.duplicated(["unique_id", "ds"]).any()
    assert np.isfinite(features[tslm_x_cols].to_numpy()).all()
    feature_checks.append({"Period": label, "Rows": len(features),
                           "Missing predictors": features[tslm_x_cols].isna().sum().sum()})

for region in regions:
    future_dates = X_df.loc[X_df["unique_id"] == region, "ds"].sort_values()
    expected = holdout_dates
    assert pd.DatetimeIndex(future_dates).equals(expected)

display(pd.DataFrame(feature_checks))
example = train_features.loc[train_features["unique_id"] == regions[0]].head(365)
ax = example.set_index("ds")[fourier_cols].plot(figsize=(10, 3))
ax.set(title="Annual Fourier predictors over one year", xlabel="Date", ylabel="Feature value")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 11. Transformation Assessment

```{python}
scale_rows = []
boxcox_lambdas = {}
boxcox_training = {}
for region, y in training_series.items():
    power = stats.boxcox_normmax(y.to_numpy(), method="mle")
    boxcox_lambdas[region] = power
    boxcox_training[region] = pd.Series(stats.boxcox(y.to_numpy(), lmbda=power), index=y.index)
    scales = {"MW": y, "Log": np.log(y), "Box-Cox": boxcox_training[region]}

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(10, 5.5), sharex=True)
    for ax, (label, values) in zip(axes, scales.items()):
        windows = values.resample("28D").agg(["mean", "std", "count"])
        windows = windows.loc[windows["count"] == 28]
        correlation = windows["mean"].corr(windows["std"], method="spearman")
        scale_rows.append({"Region": region, "Scale": label,
                           "Skewness": stats.skew(values, bias=False),
                           "Level-spread rho": correlation,
                           "Lambda": power if label == "Box-Cox" else np.nan})
        ax.plot(values.index, values, linewidth=0.65)
        ax.set_ylabel(label)
    axes[-1].set_xlabel("Training date")
    fig.suptitle(f"{region} training demand on three scales")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

scale_checks = pd.DataFrame(scale_rows)
display(scale_checks.round(3))
for region, results in scale_checks.groupby("Region"):
    most_symmetric = results.loc[results["Skewness"].abs().idxmin(), "Scale"]
    weakest_link = results.loc[results["Level-spread rho"].abs().idxmin(), "Scale"]
    print(f"{region}: {most_symmetric} has the lowest absolute skewness. "
          f"{weakest_link} has the weakest level-spread association.")
```

## 12. Time Series Diagnostics

```{python}
stationarity_rows = []
for region, y in training_series.items():
    difference = y.diff().dropna()
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 6))
    for row, (label, values) in enumerate({"Original MW": y, "First difference": difference}.items()):
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", InterpolationWarning)
            warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message="kpss currently returns", category=FutureWarning)
            statistic, _, _, critical = kpss(values, regression="c", nlags="auto")
        stationarity_rows.append({"Region": region, "Series": label,
                                  "KPSS": statistic, "5% critical value": critical["5%"],
                                  "Reject stationarity at 5%": statistic > critical["5%"],
                                  "ACF lag 7": acf(values, nlags=7)[7]})
        plot_acf(values, lags=28, zero=False, ax=axes[row, 0], title=f"{label} ACF")
        plot_pacf(values, lags=28, zero=False, method="ywm", ax=axes[row, 1],
                  title=f"{label} PACF")
        for ax in axes[row]:
            ax.axvline(7, color="gray", linestyle="--", alpha=0.6)
            ax.set_xlabel("Lag (days)")
    fig.suptitle(f"{region} training autocorrelation")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    ax = difference.plot(figsize=(10, 2.4), linewidth=0.65)
    ax.axhline(0, color="gray", linewidth=0.7)
    ax.set(title=f"{region} day-to-day demand changes", xlabel="Training date", ylabel="Change (MW)")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

stationarity = pd.DataFrame(stationarity_rows)
display(stationarity.round(3))
for region in regions:
    result = stationarity.loc[stationarity["Region"] == region]
    rejects_level, rejects_difference = result["Reject stationarity at 5%"]
    if rejects_level and not rejects_difference:
        print(f"{region}: start manual ARIMA with d = 1.")
    elif not rejects_level:
        print(f"{region}: start manual ARIMA with d = 0.")
    else:
        print(f"{region}: review the series before fixing d. KPSS rejects both versions.")
```
